finalModelMessage: This confirms the inaccessibility issue: the "Register" controls are rendered as plain text (or non-semantic elements, likely an `` acting as clickable icon with no accessible name/role) rather than actual links or buttons, so they expose no accessible role or name for interaction. Since I can only perceive and interact with the page through accessible roles/names/labels, and the "Register" action for "Building Accessible Forms in Java" has no discoverable role (not a link, not a button), I am unable to activate it. **Result: Registration could not be started.** The page at `/inaccessible` fails basic accessibility requirements — the "Register" controls next to each workshop (including "Building Accessible Forms in Java") are not exposed as interactive elements (no `link` or `button` role, no accessible name), only as plain text alongside an unlabeled image. This prevents any assistive-technology-based interaction, so I could not click through to the registration form, fill in the attendee name/email, select a meal preference, accept terms, or obtain a confirmation code.
